doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents' acceptance of his career, and his later marriage
summary: His parents were cool, his father had wanted him to be a jockey, and he married in the late 1950s after leaving Sarah Vaughan.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Your parents, by this time they’ve accepted the fact that . . .

My parents were cool a long time. My father was cool. My mother got it, because I carried myself. I didn’t get in no trouble. I never caused no problems. I’d bring home a little money. I was buying things for the house.
Your father wanted you to be a jockey. What did your mother want you to be?
You remember that, huh? My father must have thought that we were in another country, huh? He wanted me to be a jockey back – what? – in the ’30s or ’40s. I was very little. He wasn’t much bigger.
My mother, she never did preach what she wanted me to be.
Just as long as you was happy.
I guess as long as I was cool and doing – so to speak – doing the right thing.
So when did you get married?
I got married – hmm – good question – in the ’50s – late ’50s.
And then I left Sarah Vaughan.
